questions.q: How often do you use technology in your daily life?
questions.bandTip: Give a direct answer + extend with specific examples. "I use it constantly — from checking emails first thing in the morning to unwinding with streaming services at night."

questions.q: Do you think young people today rely too much on technology?
questions.bandTip: Show balance: agree partially, then nuance. Use "To some extent..." or "While I can see the argument..."

questions.q: What technology do you think has made the biggest impact on society?
questions.bandTip: Pick ONE specific technology and develop it with a reason + example. More impressive than listing several vaguely.

part2.topic: Describe a time when technology helped you solve a problem.
cuePoints: How it helped you solve it
And explain how you felt about it
part2.modelOpening: I'd like to talk about a time about two years ago when I was trying to navigate a completely unfamiliar city abroad and my phone battery had died...

questions.q: Do you think technology has made people more or less connected to each other?
questions.bandTip: Use concessive structure: "While digital platforms have undeniably expanded the reach of human connection, there is a compelling case that the depth and quality of those connections has diminished."

questions.q: Should governments regulate how technology companies use personal data?
questions.bandTip: Show awareness of complexity: individuals vs. corporations vs. state. Use "It strikes me that..." to signal a considered position.

questions.q: How do you think artificial intelligence will change the workplace in the future?
questions.bandTip: Speculate using: "It seems reasonable to anticipate...", "One can envisage a scenario in which..."

questions.q: How important is it to you to spend time in nature?
questions.bandTip: Personal + reason + example. Don't just say "I like nature" — describe a specific memory or feeling.

questions.q: Do you think people in cities are less connected to the natural world?
questions.bandTip: Partially agree + nuance. Mention urban parks, awareness campaigns as counterexamples.

questions.q: What do you do in your daily life to help the environment?
questions.bandTip: Be honest and specific. Examiners appreciate genuine answers over impressive-sounding ones.

part2.topic: Describe a natural place that has impressed you.
cuePoints: When you visited or learned about it
And explain why it left an impression on you
part2.modelOpening: The place that has most impressed me is a coastal nature reserve I visited with my family a few years ago. It was situated about three hours from where I grew up...

questions.q: Who do you think bears the greatest responsibility for environmental protection — individuals, corporations, or governments?
questions.bandTip: Avoid simplistic answers. Acknowledge all three levels then argue for your position: "While all three have a role to play, I would argue that..."

questions.q: Do you think economic development and environmental protection are compatible goals?
questions.bandTip: Use real examples: Bhutan's carbon-negative status, the EU's green industrial policy, etc.

questions.q: How has your generation's attitude towards the environment changed compared to previous generations?
questions.bandTip: Contrast using "Whereas previous generations..., my generation tends to..." Show awareness of social change.
